sections.skill: Classify fixed and variable costs and compute total cost

questions.prompt: Which is a variable cost for a bakery?

choices.text: Flour used for each batch of bread
Monthly rent for the bakery building

questions.correct_answer: Flour used for each batch of bread
questions.intro: A FIXED cost stays about the same no matter how much you sell in a period: rent, insurance, a software plan. A VARIABLE cost goes up as you sell more: ingredients, packaging, shipping, or payment fees on each sale. Example: a candle maker pays 500 dollars of rent a month (fixed) and 4 dollars of wax and jar for each candle (variable). Making 100 candles costs 500 + 4 x 100 = 900 dollars. Knowing which is which helps you plan prices and see what happens when sales change.

questions.prompt: Which is a fixed cost for an online T-shirt shop?

questions.prompt: Fixed 100, cost per item 2, items 30. What is the total?
questions.intro: Total cost often follows one pattern: total = fixed + (cost per item x number of items). Do the multiplication first, then add. Example: fixed 200, cost per item 3, items 40: 3 x 40 = 120, then 200 + 120 = 320. A common mistake is adding first: (200 + 3) x 40 is wrong. Check that the total is never less than the fixed cost.

questions.prompt: Which step comes first in "fixed + rate x quantity"?
